units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 2:3">Snh. II, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 20a:6">20ᵃ</cite>) <he>אינו יוצא מפתח פ׳ שלו</he> (Y. ed. <cite ref="Q01030"><he>פלטו׳</he></cite>, Ar. <cite ref="Q01019"><he>פלטין</he></cite>) must not leave his royal residence (to escort the dead).

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 1">Num. R. s. 1</cite> end <he>אף … ועושה אותן בני פַלְטַירִי</he> so I will bring them near me and make them sons of my palace (= <cite ref="Q01019"><he>פַּלָּטִינִי</he></cite>); [<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 695">Yalk. Num. 695</cite> <cite ref="Q01025"><he>פלטנטירין</he></cite>; Tanḥ. B’midb. 26 <he>פלמנטרין</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01084"><he>פַּלְמַנְטָר</he></cite>].
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13:2">Num. R. s. 13</cite> <he>כשתכנס … לפ׳ שלך</he> when thou enterest thy province and comest to thy headquarters.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13:2">Ib.</cite> <he>והיו בני המדינה עומדים על פתח פ׳ … יכנס המלך לפַלְטרוֹ</he> (not <he>לפלטר</he>) the citizens stood at the entrance of the palace and cried, let the king enter his palace.

<cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 3:2">Pirké d’R. El. ch. III</cite> <he>שהוא רוצה לבנות פלטרים שלו</he> (corr. <cite ref="Q01030"><he>פלטרין</he></cite>) who wishes to build his palace; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="Q01021"><he>פַּלְטֵירִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q01006"><he>פַּלְטוֹרִין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:10">Esth. R. to I, 2</cite> <he>כל אחד ואחד היו לו שני פ׳ וכ׳</he> each had two residences, one for the summer &c.; a. e.—Fem. form: <cite ref="Q01006"><he>פַּלְטוֹרָה</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q01022"><he>פַּלְטֵירָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 309:5">Sifré Deut. 309</cite> <he>פלטו׳ אחת</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 942:40">Yalk. ib. 942</cite> <he>פלטי׳</he>, v. infra.—Pl. <he>פַּלְטוֹרִיּוֹת</he>, <he>פַּלְטֵירִיאוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 942:40">Ib.</cite> <he>מי שהורישו אביו עשר פ׳ ועמד וקנה פלטורה אחת וכ׳</he> one to whom his father left ten country-seats, but he rose and bought one with his own money, and this he loved <he>מכל פ׳ שהנחילו אביו</he> (not <he>רה …</he>) more than all the residences that his father had left him.
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 353:12">Sifré Deut. 353</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 959:2">Yalk. ib. 959</cite>.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 6:3:1">Koh. R. to VI, 3</cite> <he>שתי פַלְטֵרִיּוֹת</he>, v. supra.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 71">Gen. R. s. 71</cite> <he>ירש אשר פ׳ מה וכ׳</he> (not <he>ירש גבהי</he>) Asher possessed more residences (abroad) than Judah possessed districts; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 128:1">Yalk. ib. 128</cite> <cite ref="Q01012"><he>פלטיאות</he></cite> (corr. acc.).—[<he>פלטריות</he> <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 41">Gen. R. s. 41</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="Q01011"><he>פְּלַטְיָא</he></cite>.]
